questions.passage: Did you know that one out of every ten people in the world is left-handed? They face challenges in a society <u>ⓐ designed</u> for right-handed individuals. It is inconvenient for them to use some right-handed products such as scissors, cameras, and computer mice. The world we live in is designed to be an environment <u>ⓑ suitable</u> for what is considered "normal" for the majority of people, and it is filled with objects that are easy for them to use. Thus, those who do not belong to that category have no choice but <u>ⓒ to live</u> with discomfort. In other words, a minority of people with physical differences, such as the left-handed, the disabled, and the elderly, either <u>ⓓ endures</u> inconvenience or deliberately seek objects <u>ⓔ designed</u> especially for them, which are often difficult to find.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] a minority of people ... either endures inconvenience or deliberately seek objects ... [해석] 신체적 차이가 있는 소수의 사람들은 불편을 감수하거나 특별히 그들을 위해 디자인된 물건을 일부러 찾아야 한다. 주어 'a minority of people'은 복수 취급이며, either A or B에서 동사는 주어에 수일치 → endures(3인칭 단수) ❌ → endure(복수형) ✅
det.correct:
ⓐ designed: 과거분사, a society를 수식 → '디자인된 사회' ✅
ⓑ suitable: 형용사 보어, an environment를 설명 → '적합한 환경' ✅
ⓒ to live: have no choice but to-v 구문 → ✅
ⓓ endures: 주어 a minority of people(복수) → endure여야 함 ❌ → 정답
ⓔ designed: 과거분사, objects를 뒤에서 수식 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 a minority of + 복수명사 → 복수 취급. either A or B에서 동사는 주어에 수일치. have no choice but to-v = ~할 수밖에 없다. 비교: the number of → 단수 / a number of → 복수

questions.passage: Is it impossible to build an environment where everyone can use products and facilities conveniently and without limitations? It was Ronald Mace (A) <u>[who / which]</u> sought the answer to this question. He contracted polio at the age of nine and spent the rest of his life in a wheelchair. When studying architecture at university, he struggled to access some campus facilities due to inaccessible building designs. This experience later inspired him (B) <u>[inventing / to invent]</u> the term universal design, which refers to design for all. As an architect and product designer, he pursued a world in which all products and environments (C) <u>[were designed / designed]</u> to be artistic and usable to the greatest extent possible by everyone.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] It was Ronald Mace who sought the answer / inspired him to invent / environments were designed to be artistic [해석] 이 질문의 답을 구한 사람은 바로 Ronald Mace였다. / 이 경험이 그에게 유니버설 디자인이라는 용어를 만들도록 영감을 주었다. / 모든 제품과 환경이 예술적이고 사용 가능하도록 디자인되는 세상을 추구했다.
det.correct:
(A) who: It was ~ who 강조구문, 사람 → who ✅ / which는 사물용 ❌
(B) to invent: inspire + O + to-v 구문 ✅ / inventing 불가 ❌
(C) were designed: 관계절 내 S+V 필요, 수동태 ✅ / designed만으로는 동사 없음 ❌

② (A) who – (B) to invent – (C) were designed → 모두 정확 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 It is/was ~ who/that 강조구문: 사람 → who, 사물 → which/that. inspire + O + to-v = ~에게 …하도록 영감을 주다. 관계절 내 수동태: 주어 + be p.p. 형태 필수. 비교: encourage/allow/enable + O + to-v (동일 패턴)

questions.passage: According to the principles of universal design, the design must be able to <u>ⓐ be used</u> equitably, flexibly, simply, and intuitively by a wide variety of people. In addition, it should be cognitively accessible and minimize users' physical efforts. Finally, it requires <u>ⓑ the providing</u> of sufficient space for all users while <u>ⓒ reducing</u> potential hazards and adverse consequences from accidental or unintended actions. A key feature of universal design is <u>ⓓ what</u> this is not a special requirement only for the benefit of a minority of the population.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] A key feature of universal design is what this is not a special requirement ... [해석] 유니버설 디자인의 핵심 특징은 이것이 소수만을 위한 특별 요건이 아니라는 것이다. 보어절 'this is not ~'은 완전한 절 → 접속사 that이 와야 합니다. what 뒤에는 불완전한 절이 필요하므로 부적절합니다.
det.correct:
ⓐ be used: must be able to + 동사원형(be used 수동태) ✅
ⓑ the providing: require + 명사 → 동명사의 명사적 용법 ✅
ⓒ reducing: while + v-ing(분사구문) ✅
ⓓ what: 뒤에 완전한 절(this is not ...) → that이 필요 ❌ → 정답
det.tip: 🔑 that vs. what: that + 완전한 절(S+V+O/C 갖춤) / what + 불완전한 절(주어·목적어·보어 빠짐). what = the thing that(선행사 포함 관계대명사). while + v-ing = ~하는 동안/~하면서(분사구문)

questions.passage: Clothing designed with universal design integrates stretchable and breathable materials, (A) <u>[enhancing / diminishing]</u> comfort and mobility. Other features include the use of magnets and Velcro in place of buttons, making it easier to put on and take off clothing. It also incorporates traits like stretchy waistbands and adjustable sleeves to allow individuals with disabilities to dress (B) <u>[independently / dependently]</u>. This type of clothing is also (C) <u>[beneficial / harmful]</u> for pregnant women, older adults who may experience mobility issues, and individuals with temporary injuries or medical conditions.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 문맥상 적절한 어휘를 골라 바르게 짝지은 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] 신축성·통기성 있는 소재를 결합하여 편안함을 향상시킨다. 장애인이 독립적으로 옷을 입을 수 있게 한다. 임산부에게도 유익하다. 유니버설 디자인의 목적은 편의 증진이므로 모두 긍정적 어휘가 적절합니다.
det.correct:
(A) enhancing: 편안함을 '향상' ✅ / diminishing(감소) ❌
(B) independently: '독립적으로' ✅ / dependently(의존적으로) ❌
(C) beneficial: '유익한' ✅ / harmful(해로운) ❌
① 모두 적절 → 정답 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 enhance ≈ improve, boost ↔ diminish ≈ decrease. independently ↔ dependently. beneficial ≈ helpful ↔ harmful ≈ detrimental. 유니버설 디자인 = 편리·접근성·독립성 향상 → 긍정 어휘 선택

questions.passage: Universal design is not only applied in modern architecture but also extends to transportation systems. For instance, buses have been designed with a floor closer to ground level to ① <u>ease</u> access for all passengers. Handles of various lengths are provided, another method by which universal design is implemented to ② <u>accommodate</u> passengers' different heights. Subway maps have also been designed for color-blind individuals to clearly ③ <u>confuse</u> between subway lines by adjusting the color and the brightness and by varying the thickness of lines that have similar colors. Additionally, the use of pictograms can be seen ④ <u>frequently</u>. Signs indicating the locations of subway or train stations ⑤ <u>assist</u> international travelers who may not be familiar with the local language.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] to clearly confuse between subway lines → 원문은 distinguish. [해석] 색맹인 사람이 지하철 노선을 명확하게 '혼동하다'는 문맥에 맞지 않음. '구별하다(distinguish)'가 적절합니다.
det.correct:
① ease: '용이하게 하다' → 접근을 쉽게 ✅
② accommodate: '수용하다' → 다양한 키에 맞추기 ✅
③ confuse: '혼동하다' → 구별해야 하므로 부적절 ❌ → distinguish ✅
④ frequently: '빈번하게' → 자주 보인다 ✅
⑤ assist: '돕다' → 해외 여행자를 돕는다 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 distinguish ≈ differentiate, tell apart (구별하다) ↔ confuse ≈ mix up (혼동하다). accommodate ≈ cater to (수용하다). ease ≈ facilitate (용이하게 하다). 유니버설 디자인 = 불편 감소·편의 제공 → 부정 동사(confuse)는 부적절

questions.passage: Inclusive language is a ① <u>respectful</u> way of communication by selecting words that avoid bias, prejudice, and discrimination. Inclusive language promotes equality, respect, and diversity, ② <u>inviting</u> all people to participate in society. For example, replacing conventional terms with racial implications like "blacklist" and "whitelist" with ③ <u>neutral</u> alternatives such as "deny list" and "allow list" enhances inclusivity. Similarly, using gender-neutral terms like "parent" and "guardian" instead of "mom" and "dad" helps break down biases and ④ <u>reinforces</u> diverse family structures. Moreover, it is crucial to be aware of everyday phrases that could be considered ⑤ <u>insensitive</u> toward individuals with medical conditions.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] helps break down biases and reinforces diverse family structures → 원문은 acknowledges. [해석] 편견을 해소하고 다양한 가족 구조를 '강화한다' → '인정한다(acknowledges)'가 원문 표현이며 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.correct:
① respectful: '존중하는' → 적절 ✅
② inviting: '초대하는' → 참여를 권유 ✅
③ neutral: '중립적인' → 중립적 대안 ✅
④ reinforces: '강화하다' → 원문 acknowledges(인정하다) ❌ → 정답
⑤ insensitive: '배려 없는' → 적절 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 acknowledge ≈ recognize, accept (인정하다) ↔ reinforce ≈ strengthen (강화하다). 포용적 언어의 핵심 = 다양성 '인정'. break down biases = 편견 해소. inclusive ≈ embracing ↔ exclusive

questions.passage: Is it impossible to build an environment where everyone can use products and facilities conveniently and without limitations? It was Ronald Mace who sought the answer to this question. He contracted polio at the age of nine and spent the rest of his life in a wheelchair. When studying architecture at university, he struggled to access some campus facilities due to inaccessible building designs. This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design, which refers to design for all. As an architect and product designer, he pursued a world in which all products and environments were designed to be artistic and usable to the greatest extent possible by everyone, regardless of their age, size, disability, nationality, or language.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] 이 글은 Ronald Mace의 경험이 유니버설 디자인 용어 탄생의 계기가 되었고, 모든 사람을 위한 디자인이라는 목적을 설명합니다. 핵심 키워드: universal design, for all, everyone.
det.correct:
① 유니버설 디자인의 기원과 모든 사람을 위한 목적 → 글 전체를 관통 ✅
② 소아마비 환자의 일상 어려움 → 부분적 내용 ❌
③ 건축가로서의 경력 성과 → 핵심이 아님 ❌
④ 대학 건물 접근성 기준의 역사 → 세부 소재일 뿐 ❌
⑤ 사회 변화를 위한 건축 공부 → 요지와 거리 있음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 주제 찾기: 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심 키워드 → 'universal design', 'for all'. 부분적 내용 vs. 전체 주제 구별. regardless of = ~에 관계없이

questions.passage: How has universal design been incorporated into modern architecture? One of the most representative examples of universal design being used to improve accessibility is the ramps installed in front of buildings. Ramps, not stairs, are necessary for people with disabilities who use wheelchairs, and they are also beneficial for parents pushing strollers and the elderly. Another example is automatic doors. They are invaluable for those who rely on assistive devices such as wheelchairs and crutches. They also provide convenience for adults who have their hands full and children who are not tall enough to open the doors themselves. A further example is tactile paving. These textured surfaces, often found on sidewalks, steps, and crosswalks, assist visually impaired individuals by guiding them through urban spaces.

det.ref: [해석] 유니버설 디자인이 현대 건축에 적용된 세 가지 사례(경사로, 자동문, 점자 블록)를 설명합니다. 작은 설계 변화가 모두에게 큰 영향을 줍니다.

① 건축에서의 유니버설 디자인: 작은 변화, 큰 영향 → 전체를 아우름 ✅
② 경사로만 다룸 → 범위 좁음 ❌
③ 스마트 빌딩 기술 → 언급 없음 ❌
④ 보조 장치 → 부분적 ❌
⑤ 점자 블록만 다룸 → 범위 좁음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 제목: 포괄적 + 핵심 키워드 포함. 여러 사례를 모두 포함할 수 있는 상위 개념 선택. representative ≈ typical. invaluable ≈ extremely valuable

④ objects: '반대하다' → 문맥 무관 ❌
⑤ withdraws: '철수하다' → 문맥 무관 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 빈칸 추론: 앞뒤 논리 흐름 파악. 'not only for a minority' → 'everyone benefits'. benefit ≈ profit, gain. If(긍정 조건) → 긍정 결과

questions.passage: Did you know that one out of every ten people in the world is left-handed? They face challenges in a society designed for right-handed individuals. It is inconvenient for them to use some right-handed products such as scissors, cameras, and computer mice. The world we live in is designed to be an environment suitable for what is considered "normal" for the majority of people, and it is filled with objects that are easy for them to use. Thus, those who do not belong to that category have no choice but to live with discomfort. In other words, ______________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 문장으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] In other words, a minority of people ... either endure inconvenience or deliberately seek objects designed especially for them [해석] 즉, 신체적 차이가 있는 소수는 불편을 감수하거나 특별 디자인 물건을 찾아야 한다. 'In other words'는 앞 내용을 바꿔 말하는 연결어입니다.
det.correct:
① 소수가 불편 감수 또는 특별 물건 탐색 → 앞 문장 'discomfort' 구체화 ✅
② 왼손잡이가 배워야 한다 → 글의 논지(환경이 문제)와 반대 ❌
③ 대다수도 불만 → '소수'의 불편 강조와 맞지 않음 ❌
④ 의도적 배제 → 'intentionally' 과장 ❌
⑤ 신체적 차이 감소 → 지문에 없는 내용 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 In other words = 다시 말해서(앞 내용 재진술). endure ≈ tolerate, bear. deliberately ≈ intentionally. minority ↔ majority. 빈칸(문장): 연결어에 주목하여 논리 흐름 파악

ch: a minority of people with physical differences either endure inconvenience or deliberately seek specially designed objects
left-handed people should learn to use right-handed products to avoid inconvenience
the majority of people are also dissatisfied with the current design standards
most products are intentionally designed to exclude certain groups of people
physical differences among people are decreasing due to modern technology

questions.passage: You may find it surprising that universal design can be found in more parts of society than you thought. However, enough has not been done to accommodate everyone yet. Universal design should be implemented more extensively to promote full participation in the community for a wider range of people. It is time to build more equitable environments that are accessible to everyone. <u>So are you on board to create a universally designed world for all?</u>
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "So are you on board to create a universally designed world for all?"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] So are you on board to create a universally designed world for all? [해석] 모두를 위해 유니버설하게 디자인된 세상을 만드는 데 동참할 의향이 있나요? 'on board'는 '참여하다, 동참하다'라는 관용 표현입니다.
det.correct:
① 세상을 모두에게 접근 가능하게 만드는 노력에 동참 → on board의 의미 + 맥락 일치 ✅
② 이미 완전히 달성 → 'enough has not been done' 모순 ❌
③ 차량으로 여행 → 'on board'를 '탑승'으로 오해 ❌
④ 편의 포기 → 편의 확대가 핵심 ❌
⑤ 이론적 개념 → 실제 적용 사례 다수 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 on board = willing to participate. get on board = 참여하다. 함축 문제: ① 관용 표현 의미 파악 ② 글 전체 맥락에서 필자 의도 확인

ch: Are you willing to participate in the effort to make the world accessible to everyone?
Do you agree that universal design has already been fully achieved?
Would you like to travel around the world on a universally designed vehicle?
Are you ready to give up convenience for the sake of universal design?
Do you think universal design is only a theoretical concept?

questions.passage:
[주어진 글] While universal design has been utilized in architecture and transportation systems for some time, a newer application is in the fashion industry.

(A) It also incorporates traits like stretchy waistbands and adjustable sleeves to allow individuals with disabilities to dress independently.

(B) Clothing designed with universal design integrates stretchable and breathable materials, enhancing comfort and mobility. Other features include the use of magnets and Velcro in place of buttons, making it easier to put on and take off clothing.

(C) This type of clothing is also beneficial for pregnant women, older adults who may experience mobility issues, and individuals with temporary injuries or medical conditions.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] 주어진 글: 패션 산업 적용 → (B) 소재·특징 소개 → (A) 'It also'로 추가 특징 → (C) 'This type of clothing'으로 종합 혜택
det.correct:
① (A)–(B)–(C): 'It also'가 갑자기 나옴 ❌
② (A)–(C)–(B): 'It also'가 부자연스러움 ❌
③ (B)–(A)–(C): 소재→추가특징→종합 혜택 → 자연스러운 흐름 ✅
④ (B)–(C)–(A): (C) 뒤 'It also' 어색 ❌
⑤ (C)–(B)–(A): 'This type' 선행 없음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 순서배열: 지시어 추적! 'It also' → 앞에 이미 설명 필요. 'This type of clothing' → 앞에 의류 특징 설명 필요. 논리 흐름: 도입→구체적 특징→추가→종합

questions.passage: How has universal design been incorporated into modern architecture? ① One of the most representative examples of universal design being used to improve accessibility is the ramps installed in front of buildings. ② Ramps, not stairs, are necessary for people with disabilities who use wheelchairs, and they are also beneficial for parents pushing strollers and the elderly. ③ The history of ramp construction dates back to ancient Egypt, where ramps were used to build pyramids. ④ Another example is automatic doors, which are invaluable for those who rely on assistive devices such as wheelchairs and crutches. ⑤ They also provide convenience for adults who have their hands full and children who are not tall enough to open the doors themselves.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오.

det.ref: [해석] ③ 경사로 건설의 역사가 고대 이집트까지 거슬러 올라간다 → 유니버설 디자인의 현대 건축 적용이라는 글의 흐름과 무관합니다.
det.correct:
① 유니버설 디자인 사례로 경사로 → 흐름 부합 ✅
② 경사로의 혜택 → 흐름 부합 ✅
③ 고대 이집트 경사로 역사 → 현대 건축과 무관 ❌ → 정답
④ 자동문 사례 → 흐름 부합 ✅
⑤ 자동문의 편의 → 흐름 부합 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 무관문장: 핵심 키워드(universal design + modern architecture)에서 벗어나는 문장 찾기. '고대 이집트'는 '현대 건축' 범위를 벗어남. date back to = ~까지 거슬러 올라가다

questions.passage: It was Ronald Mace who sought the answer to this question. He contracted polio at the age of nine and spent the rest of his life in a wheelchair. When studying architecture at university, he struggled to access some campus facilities due to inaccessible building designs. This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design, which refers to design for all.
questions.stem:
다음 내용이 본문과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

「Ronald Mace invented the term "universal design" before he contracted polio.」

det.ref: [원문] He contracted polio at the age of nine ... This experience later inspired him to invent the term [해석] 9살에 소아마비 → 이후 유니버설 디자인 용어 발명. '소아마비 전에 만들었다'는 거짓(F).
det.correct:
시간순: 소아마비(9세) → 대학 → 접근성 문제 경험 → 용어 발명
'before he contracted polio'는 사실과 반대 → F ✅
det.tip: 🔑 T/F: 시간 순서 주의! contract = (병에) 걸리다. 'later inspired' → '이후에' 영감. 소아마비가 먼저, 용어 발명이 나중

questions.passage: As an architect and product designer, he pursued a world in which all products and environments were designed to be artistic and usable to the greatest extent possible by everyone, regardless of their age, size, disability, nationality, or language. ... It is time to build more equitable environments that are accessible to everyone.
questions.stem:
다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

[조건] 본문에 등장하는 영단어 1개로 쓸 것
[보기] accessible, equitable, universal

The ultimate goal of universal design is to build a more ( ) world for all.

det.ref: [원문] build more equitable environments that are accessible to everyone. [해석] 모두에게 접근 가능한 더 공평한 환경을 만들 때이다. 보기 중 원문 마지막 단락의 핵심 형용사는 equitable입니다.
det.correct:
equitable: 원문 'build more equitable environments'에서 가져온 핵심 형용사 → 정답 ✅
accessible: 본문에 등장하나 'more equitable'이 원문 표현과 더 일치
universal: 'more universal'이라는 표현은 원문에 없음
det.tip: 🔑 equitable ≈ fair, just (공평한) ↔ inequitable ≈ unfair. 요약형 서술: 보기 단어를 본문에서 찾아 문맥 대조. 'a more' + 형용사 비교급 구문

questions.passage: When studying architecture at university, he struggled to access some campus facilities due to inaccessible building designs. This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design, which refers to design for all.
questions.stem:
다음 조건에 맞게 주어진 단어를 활용하여 영작하시오.

[조건]
• 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하되 필요시 형태를 변형할 것
• 본문의 내용에 근거하여 한 문장으로 작성할 것

[보기] inspire / he / invent / the term / universal design

det.ref: [원문] This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design. [해석] 이 경험이 나중에 그에게 유니버설 디자인이라는 용어를 발명하도록 영감을 주었다.
det.correct:
핵심 구문: inspire + 목적어(him) + to-v(to invent)
주어: This/The/His experience
동사: inspired (과거형)
목적어: the term universal design
det.tip: 🔑 inspire + O + to-v = ~에게 …하도록 영감을 주다. 비교: encourage/motivate/persuade + O + to-v. 시제: 과거 사건 → inspired. 조건의 모든 단어 사용 확인

questions.passage: Overall, universal design clothing promotes increased comfort, convenience, independence, and improved mobility and flexibility for wearers of all abilities.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

Universal design clothing promotes increased comfort, convenience, independence, and improved mobility and flexibility for wearers of all ( ). [able]

det.ref: [원문] for wearers of all abilities. [해석] 모든 능력을 가진 착용자를 위해. able(형용사) → ability(명사) → abilities(복수형). 전치사 of 뒤에 명사 + all 뒤에 복수명사.
det.correct:
able (형용사) → ability (명사) → abilities (복수형)
전치사 of + 명사 필요 / all + 복수명사
of all abilities = 모든 능력 수준의
det.tip: 🔑 able(형) → ability(명) → abilities(복수). 전치사 of 뒤에 명사(구). all + 복수명사. of all abilities = regardless of abilities
